goals: Mechanistic: quantify partitioning of precipitation into surface runoff, ET, and recharge across the Naches and attribute it to elevation/orographic-forcing and soil-texture gradients
Validation: compare simulated SWE and water-table depth against in-domain observations; assess streamflow feasibility
drivers_to_resolve: elevation (orographic precip + rain-snow transition via NLDAS)

model_choice.rationale: Single-column ELM resolves the full water balance (ET, runoff, drainage, snow) at each point; CONUS NLDAS forcing makes the elevation/orographic gradient a real, resolvable axis in this high-relief basin.

answerable: Soil-texture control on runoff/ET/recharge partitioning (native SSURGO lever)
Elevation/orographic-forcing control on partitioning and snow (NLDAS varies precip/temp with elevation across this 1625 m-relief CONUS basin)
SWE validation against SNOTEL (snow is in default history output)
Water-table-depth validation against USGS wells (with WTD-informed warm start)

not_answerable.aspect: Validation of partitioning against the 93 USGS stream gauges
not_answerable.why: Single-column ELM has no lateral transport or routing; column runoff cannot be integrated into gauge streamflow
12 km NLDAS cells average over sub-grid terrain, biasing high-elevation SWE low

sampling_strategy.approach: stratified (elevation bands x dominant soil classes), with validation columns pinned to observation sites
sampling_strategy.n_justification: 4 elevation bands x 3 dominant soil textures = 12 columns spans the two primary partitioning controls with one column per stratum; the rain-snow transition band is prioritized for placement. No dense grid — 12 is the smallest set resolving both axes.
sampling_strategy.placement_logic: Concentrate columns in the rain-snow transition (750-1200 m) where snow-vs-rain partitioning and recharge timing are most sensitive, and oversample valley-bottom/riparian corridors where soil-moisture-to-recharge exchange is strongest; distribute remaining columns to cover coarse vs fine soils in each band.
sampling_strategy.replication: None in baseline; strata themselves provide contrast. Light replication in the transition band can be added if forcing-cell variance is high.

sampling_plan.reason: Rain-dominated low elevation: isolates soil-texture control on runoff vs recharge where snow is minimal.
Most climatically sensitive band; isolates how mixed rain/snow forcing partitions into ET, runoff, and recharge across textures.
Snowmelt-driven recharge/runoff regime; tests seasonal storage-and-release partitioning.
Deep snowpack end-member for the elevation gradient; anchors the orographic precip/SWE response.

validation_design.comparison: co-located — place/validate columns at the 6 SNOTEL sites; compare simulated peak SWE and melt timing
co-located — columns pinned to wells; requires Fan-2013 WTD-informed warm start; expect drift vs Fan lateral equilibrium (a reportable result)
validation_design.n_validation_points: unknown — depends on well density in HUC 17030002

validation_design.comparison: NOT feasible as posed — no routing/aggregation of column runoff to gauge; flagged as gap

experiment_summary.primary_treatment: default NLDAS-2 forcing, native SSURGO soil, Fan-2013 WTD-informed warm start + short spin-up

requires_capabilities.why: convert independent column surface+subsurface runoff into basin/reach streamflow
requires_capabilities.blocks: validation against the 93 USGS stream gauges

requires_capabilities.why: NLDAS 12 km cells average over Cascade terrain and bias ridgetop precip/SWE
requires_capabilities.blocks: accurate high-elevation SWE and orographic partitioning detail

requires_capabilities.capability: Fan-2013 WTD-informed warm start + multi-year spin-up
requires_capabilities.why: recharge and ZWT are initialization artifacts from a cold start
requires_capabilities.blocks: meaningful recharge quantification and WTD validation

requires_capabilities.capability: DEM/elevation raster sampling + SSURGO soil raster sampling
requires_capabilities.why: expander needs real elevation and soil to place stratified columns
requires_capabilities.blocks: converting strata rules into concrete points

requires_capabilities.capability: SNOTEL and USGS-well observation ingest with co-location resolver
requires_capabilities.why: pin validation columns to station coordinates

assumptions: Naches is fully within CONUS, so NLDAS-2 elevation-resolved forcing applies to all columns.
SSURGO soil coverage is complete across the basin and reducible to ~3 dominant texture classes.
USGS wells with usable WTD records exist within the HUC; count and depth suitability unknown until data query.
Recharge is interpreted as ELM sub-surface drainage/recharge flux (QDRAI/QRECHARGE), not a lateral-flow water balance.
Baseline forcing period is a multi-year window within 1980-2018 including spin-up years; exact years set downstream.
open_questions: How many USGS wells in-domain have WTD records suitable for co-located validation?
Which multi-year forcing window (and how many spin-up years) best matches the SNOTEL/well observation periods?
Is a future routing/aggregation capability planned so the 93 gauges can eventually be used?
Should the transition band receive replication to capture NLDAS forcing-cell variance?
